clue.text: Revolutionary, with total recanting, to become less miserable

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary

indicators.note: to recant is to take back one's words, so the word for total is read backwards

parts.note: pure, as in 'pure nonsense', means total

explanation.surface: A revolutionary cheers up by taking back every word he has said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recanting', taking one's words back, tells you to read the word for total backwards; total means pure as in 'pure nonsense'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer up is to grow brighter in spirits, which is becoming less miserable.

clue.text: Fruit course is announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word sounds like the one entered

parts.note: a current is a flow or course, as of a river

explanation.surface: The fruit course is declared on the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: A currant is a small dried grape, or a berry such as blackcurrant.

clue.text: Eject from one-time Greek island

parts.note: ex means former or one-time
Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: Someone is thrown out of a former Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: To excrete is to expel waste from the body, so to discharge or eject.

clue.text: Marsupials must finally settle for the night

parts.note: roos is short for kangaroos, which are marsupials

indicators.note: finally means only the closing letter of must is used

explanation.surface: Kangaroos eventually have to bed down for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds roost when they perch to sleep, so to settle down for the night.

clue.text: Fellow secures new help to advancement for clerk in a dull job

indicators.note: secures means holds fast, so the fellow encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a peer is a fellow or equal
a push is a helping shove forward

explanation.surface: A colleague gets a fresh boost up the ladder for a bored clerk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secures' has the fellow holding the other two pieces inside it; peer means an equal, a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen-pusher is a derogatory term for an office worker doing routine paperwork.

clue.text: Chests of principally charitable things given

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, so only the leading letter of charitable is taken

parts.note: offers are things given or held out to someone

explanation.surface: Charity donations go into chests.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffers are strongboxes, so chests in the sense of containers for valuables.

clue.text: Break up constant torture

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
the rack is an instrument of torture, and to rack is to torture

explanation.surface: Constant torture causes a breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack is to split or break apart, so to break up.

clue.text: Steer around south of France, see upcoming type of race

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means below, so the steer letters follow France
around means turned about, so the letters of steer are rearranged
in a down clue, upcoming means reading upwards, so the see is written backwards

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, the seat of a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Steering round the south of France, with a see coming up, in a kind of race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges steer into REEST; 'upcoming' reads the see upwards to give YLE. Ely, a cathedral city, is the usual crossword see.
explanation.definitionFit: A freestyle race is a swimming event where any stroke may be used.

clue.text: Ban insane mob rage

indicators.note: insane suggests something deranged, so the letters of mob rage are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ban on mad mob anger.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official prohibition, especially on trade.

clue.text: Comfort gullible type on the radio

indicators.note: words on the radio are heard, so the answer sounds like the word for a gullible type

parts.note: a sucker is a gullible person

explanation.surface: A gullible person seeks comfort on a radio show.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour is help or aid given in time of need, so solace or comfort.

clue.text: Motoring organisation swindle takes in old masked dustbin-scavenger

parts.note: the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

indicators.note: takes in means holds inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a con is a swindle

explanation.surface: A breakdown service pulls a scam on an old scavenger of bins.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC (Royal Automobile Club) is a British roadside breakdown service.
explanation.definitionFit: The raccoon has a black mask-like face marking and is notorious for raiding rubbish bins.

clue.text: Harsh and bitter bishop in command, pursuing one regime at first

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the bishop and command pieces come after the others

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards and dice

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of regime is used

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
IC is the abbreviation for in charge or in command

explanation.surface: A bishop in charge follows a one-man regime with harsh, bitter results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pursuing' means the bishop and command pieces come last, behind one and regime's first letter, though the clue names them first.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbic describes a sharp, sour tone or taste, matching both senses of harsh and bitter.

clue.text: Amazed as we crashed lorry

indicators.note: crashed suggests something smashed and rearranged, so the letters of as we are mixed up

parts.note: a truck is the American word for a British lorry

explanation.surface: Onlookers are stunned as a lorry crashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Awestruck means filled with wonder, so stunned or amazed.

clue.text: Motor found dumped in reservoir

indicators.note: something dumped in the reservoir is found lying inside the word, so the answer sits within its letters

explanation.surface: A motor is discovered dumped in a reservoir.
explanation.definitionFit: A servo is a servomotor, a small motor that controls a mechanism.

clue.text: Letter of thanks after article

indicators.note: after means following, so the thanks piece goes behind the article

parts.note: the is the definite article
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A thank-you letter written after a newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts thanks behind the article; ta is informal British for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Four in a spacious car pass summer lethargically

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the numeral goes within the car

parts.note: an estate is a British car with a large load area, like a station wagon
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people in a roomy car while away the summer lazily.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: To aestivate is to spend summer in a dormant state, as some animals do.

clue.text: 60 minutes for Disney dwarf when drinks are half-price?

parts.note: Happy is one of the seven dwarfs in Disney's Snow White
an hour is sixty minutes

explanation.surface: An hour set aside for a cheerful dwarf, during cheap drinks in the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy hour is the period when a bar sells drinks at reduced prices; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Burning obsession of European republic supporting gutless policy

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting underneath, so the republic follows the other piece
gutless means with the insides removed, so only the outer letters of policy remain

parts.note: Romania is a republic in eastern Europe

explanation.surface: A European republic propping up a feeble policy becomes obsessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutless' leaves PY from policy, and 'supporting' puts ROMANIA beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyromania is a compulsion to set fires, literally an obsession with burning.

clue.text: Record-keeper in golf hemmed in by a stirrer, deplorably

indicators.note: hemmed in by means surrounded, so the golf letter goes inside the other letters
deplorably suggests something done badly, so the letters of a stirrer are jumbled

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A record-keeper at the golf club is shamefully surrounded by a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deplorably' rearranges A STIRRER into RESITRAR, and 'hemmed in by' puts G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A registrar is an official who keeps registers of births, marriages and deaths or other records.

clue.text: Religious instruction at heart polemises in a lower degree, lacking a frame

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for religious instruction, a British school subject

indicators.note: at heart means the central letter of polemises is taken

parts.note: less means to a lower degree

explanation.surface: Religious teaching argues less fiercely and lacks structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimless glasses have no rim, that is no frame round the lenses.

clue.text: Nonsense initially attracts wonderfully sonorous boisterous laughs

parts.note: guff is informal for nonsense

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each of the next words is taken

explanation.surface: Nonsense draws wonderfully loud, rowdy laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A guffaw is a loud, hearty laugh.

clue.text: Present object having zero weight?

parts.note: an end is an object or aim
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Is a present weightless?
explanation.walkthrough: Present is a verb here, to give.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give money or a quality to someone, so to present or bestow.

clue.text: Become dejected and react when Democrat replaces Republican

indicators.note: the US party abbreviations D and R, Democrat taking the Republican's place in the word

parts.note: to respond is to react

explanation.surface: How voters react when a Democrat replaces a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when Democrat replaces Republican' swaps the R of RESPOND for D.
explanation.definitionFit: To despond is to lose heart, an old verb meaning become dejected.

clue.text: Naughty new dog going round heart of lairs gets duck

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so the dog letters surround the other piece
naughty suggests misbehaving, so the letters of new dog are jumbled
heart of means the central letter of lairs

explanation.surface: A naughty new dog circles the dens and catches a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' rearranges NEW DOG into WDGEON, and 'going round' wraps it round I from lairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The widgeon, or wigeon, is a species of wild dabbling duck.

clue.text: Civilian expounder of Muslim law

definitions.meaning: ... is civilian clothes worn by someone usually in uniform, so in ... means dressed as a civilian
a Muslim legal scholar who gives rulings on Islamic law

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both plain clothes worn off duty and an Islamic jurist who interprets sharia.

clue.text: Female dish, lacking restraints, with base need finally, had amorous affairs

parts.note: a woman is a female

indicators.note: restraints are the bounds at either end, so dish loses its outer letters

parts.note: E is the base of natural logarithms

indicators.note: finally means only the closing letter of need is used

explanation.surface: An unrestrained dish of a woman had flings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking restraints' strips D and H from dish, leaving IS; 'finally' takes D from need.
explanation.definitionFit: To womanise is to pursue many casual love affairs with women, here in the past tense.

clue.text: Start of welcome warmth produces cereal crop

indicators.note: start of means only the opening letter of welcome is used

parts.note: heat is warmth

explanation.surface: A warm welcome makes the grain grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheat is a cereal grass grown for its grain, used for flour.

clue.text: Circling in Iran, a unit of currency

indicators.note: circling in suggests letters spun round, so the letters of Iran and a are rearranged

explanation.surface: A currency circulating in Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circling in' rearranges the letters of Iran into NAIR, and the A is kept at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The naira is the currency of Nigeria.

clue.text: European fellow upset issue

parts.note: a man is a fellow
ate means upset or worried, as in 'what's eating him?'

explanation.surface: A European man is upset about an issue.
explanation.walkthrough: Eat can mean to worry or trouble, so its past tense ate stands for upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue as a verb means flow out or come forth, which is what emanate means.

clue.text: Racket involving mystic syllable is harmful to health

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so the syllable goes inside the racket

parts.note: a racket is a din, a noise
om is the sacred syllable chanted in Hindu and Buddhist meditation

explanation.surface: Chanting a mystic syllable makes a racket that harms your health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' has the racket wrapped round the syllable; noisome is unrelated to noise despite the look.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means noxious or offensive, so harmful or unwholesome.

clue.text: Drunkenly cuss pet believed to be guilty of misdeed

definitions.text: believed to be guilty of misdeed

indicators.note: drunkenly suggests staggering out of order, so the letters of cuss pet are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone swearing at a pet while drunk is thought guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: To be suspect, or a suspect, is to be thought guilty of a crime or wrongdoing.

clue.text: Adult group working in desert

parts.note: A is the film classification for adult
a band is a group
on means working or operating

explanation.surface: A grown-up band plays in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: Desert is a verb here, to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon is to leave behind or forsake, the verb sense of desert.
